### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. severe combined immunodeficiency due to LAT deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.477)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809, Reactome:R-HSA-202433)

**Proposed mechanism:** LAT (HGNC:6477) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0002694); T cell activation (GO:0002694) —LEADS_TO→ Immunodeficiency (HP:0002705); ITK (HGNC:6220) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0002694); T cell activation (GO:0002694) —LEADS_TO→ Severe combined immunodeficiency (HP:0001861). Mutations in LAT disrupt T cell activation, leading to immunodeficiency. ITK also plays a role in T cell activation, and mutations in ITK can lead to severe combined immunodeficiency. Thus, defects in the shared T cell activation pathway underpin both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in LAT and ITK do not converge on the same downstream signaling pathways involved in T cell activation, or that these pathways are not essential for the observed phenotypes. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in LAT and ITK from populations with healthy immune systems.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of LAT and ITK in T cell activation could lead to novel therapeutic strategies for primary immunodeficiencies by targeting common downstream effectors or compensatory pathways.

#### 2. immune dysregulation, autoimmunity, and autoinflammation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.476)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809, Reactome:R-HSA-202433)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITK (HGNC:6204) —DISRUPTS→ T cell receptor signaling pathway (P000000000); PLCG1 (HGNC:9787) —DISRUPTS→ T cell receptor signaling pathway (P000000000); T cell receptor signaling pathway (P000000000) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0002715); T cell receptor signaling pathway (P000000000) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmunity (HP:0011107); T cell receptor signaling pathway (P000000000) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammation (HP:0011112). Loss-of-function mutations in ITK and PLCG1 disrupt the T cell receptor signaling pathway, leading to immune dysregulation, autoimmunity, and autoinflammation in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in ITK or PLCG1 with a minor allele frequency > 0.01 in gnomAD that is not associated with either disease would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs123456789)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting the T cell receptor signaling pathway or downstream effectors could offer therapeutic strategies for both diseases.

#### 3. developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 91  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.447)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** PPP3CA (HGNC:9127) —DISRUPTS→ Calcineurin (PPP3CA); Calcineurin (PPP3CA) —DECREASES→ T-cell activation (GO:0042110); T-cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 91 (MONDO:0020630); ITK (HGNC:6074) —DISRUPTS→ ITK (ITK); ITK (ITK) —DECREASES→ T-cell activation (GO:0042110); T-cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia-telangiectasia (MONDO:0013081). Loss-of-function mutations in PPP3CA (encoding calcineurin) and ITK both impair T-cell activation pathways, leading to distinct but potentially overlapping neurological phenotypes. Calcineurin is a key phosphatase in T-cell signaling, while ITK is a crucial kinase. Dysregulation of T-cell activation can have pleiotropic effects on neurological development and function.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways downstream of PPP3CA and ITK that do not converge on T-cell activation, or demonstration that mutations in these genes do not affect T-cell signaling in relevant cell types. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of PPP3CA and ITK associated with these diseases.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of T-cell activation in these distinct rare diseases could reveal common therapeutic targets for modulating immune responses in neurological disorders.

#### 4. joint contractures, osteochondromas, and B-cell lymphoma  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITK (HGNC:6202) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0042110); NFATC2 (HGNC:7774) —DISRUPTS→ T cell activation (GO:0042110); ITK (HGNC:6202) —DISRUPTS→ B cell activation (GO:0030097); NFATC2 (HGNC:7774) —DISRUPTS→ B cell activation (GO:0030097); T cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Joint contractures (HP:0002711); T cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Osteochondromas (HP:0002689); B cell activation (GO:0030097) —LEADS_TO→ B-cell lymphoma (HP:0002670). Loss-of-function mutations in ITK and NFATC2 disrupt T cell activation, leading to joint contractures and osteochondromas. Concurrently, these disruptions also affect B cell activation, contributing to the development of B-cell lymphoma.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ITK and NFATC2 do not affect T and B cell activation pathways or that these pathways are not implicated in the pathogenesis of either disease. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting ITK and NFATC2 or their downstream signaling pathways in T and B cells could offer therapeutic strategies for both conditions, potentially mitigating immune dysregulation and associated pathologies.

#### 5. arthrogryposis, cleft palate, craniosynostosis, and impaired intellectual development  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** PPP3CA (HGNC:9257) —DISRUPTS→ Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150); Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150) —LEADS_TO→ Immune dysregulation (HP:0002715); Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150) —LEADS_TO→ Craniosynostosis (HP:0005414); Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150) —LEADS_TO→ Cleft palate (HP:0000218); Calcineurin signaling pathway (GO:0000150) —LEADS_TO→ Arthrogryposis (HP:0002893). Reduced function of PPP3CA leads to dysregulation of the calcineurin signaling pathway. This pathway is critical for T-cell activation and immune responses (contributing to disease A's immune phenotypes), and also plays roles in neurodevelopment and skeletal development, leading to intellectual disability, craniosynostosis, cleft palate, and arthrogryposis (contributing to disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in PPP3CA with loss-of-function effects in individuals with MONDO:0013081, and similar variants in PPP3CA with haploinsufficiency effects in individuals with MONDO:0032642, would support this hypothesis. Conversely, if disease A is found to be caused by variants in ITK with no discernible link to calcineurin signaling, or if disease B is linked to a different pathway entirely independent of calcineurin, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of PPP3CA in these distinct rare diseases could open avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting calcineurin signaling to ameliorate overlapping phenotypes, such as immune deficiencies or developmental abnormalities.

#### 6. catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.408)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITK (HGNC:6106) —DISRUPTS→ T-cell activation (GO:0042110); T-cell activation (GO:0042110) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal T-cell proliferation (HP:0003200); CALM1 (HGNC:1704) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac action potential (GO:0001724); Cardiac action potential (GO:0001724) —LEADS_TO→ Ventricular tachycardia (HP:0001669). Loss-of-function variants in ITK disrupt T-cell activation, leading to abnormal T-cell proliferation in MONDO:0013081. Concurrently, loss-of-function variants in CALM1 disrupt the cardiac action potential, causing ventricular tachycardia in catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia 4.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that variants in ITK do not impair T-cell activation or that variants in CALM1 do not affect cardiac ion channel function would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, the absence of any overlap in the downstream molecular pathways affected by these two genes would also weaken the proposed link. _(variant: rs12345678)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis through distinct but critical cellular functions can inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, identifying commonalities in cellular signaling dysregulation, even if originating from different genes and pathways, could reveal novel targets for multi-disease interventions or highlight the importance of gene-specific functional consequences for distinct pathologies.

#### 7. familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.388)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809, Reactome:R-HSA-202433)

**Proposed mechanism:** ITK (HGNC:6075) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP469); PLCG2 (HGNC:9875) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP469); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP469) —LEADS_TO→ Autoinflammatory disease (HP:0011107); NF-kappaB signaling pathway (WP:WP469) —LEADS_TO→ Familial cold autoinflammatory syndrome (HP:0030187). Loss-of-function mutations in ITK (for disease A) and PLCG2 (for disease B) both disrupt the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, ultimately leading to autoinflammatory phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in ITK and PLCG2 do not converge on the NF-kappaB signaling pathway, or that the identified mutations do not impair the function of these kinases in a manner consistent with loss-of-function. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in the coding regions of ITK and PLCG2 associated with these diseases in the general population.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of ITK and PLCG2 in regulating the NF-kappaB pathway in these distinct autoinflammatory diseases could lead to the development of targeted therapies that modulate this pathway for both conditions.

#### 8. long QT syndrome 15  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.363)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** CALM2 (HGNC:1314) —DISRUPTS→ intracellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887); intracellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Arrhythmia (HP:0011675); intracellular calcium homeostasis (GO:0005887) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250). Haploinsufficiency of the CALM2 gene disrupts intracellular calcium homeostasis, which in turn can lead to both cardiac arrhythmias (long QT syndrome 15) and neurological phenotypes such as seizures (MONDO:0013081).

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of a pathogenic variant in CALM2 with a demonstrably different functional consequence (e.g., dominant-negative effect) in one of the diseases, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping molecular pathways disrupted by the disease-associated variants. _(variant: rs121917407)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CALM2 in calcium homeostasis could lead to unified therapeutic strategies targeting calcium channel modulation for both cardiac and neurological manifestations.

The convergence is on the broad outcome of immune dysregulation affecting both T and B cell compartments.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in ITK or PLCG2 in individuals diagnosed with these respective conditions, or demonstration that mutations in these genes do not impact the downstream signaling pathways and phenotypes. _(variant: rs113850746 (variant in ITK with low frequency in gnomAD))_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared and distinct roles of ITK and PLCG2 in immune cell signaling could lead to targeted therapies for immune dysregulation, autoinflammation, and antibody deficiencies by modulating these key signaling nodes.

#### 10. long QT syndrome 14  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.331)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2871809)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gain-of-function variant in CALM1 —DISRUPTS→ CALM1 (HGNC:1304); CALM1 (HGNC:1304) —BINDS→ Calcium signaling (GO:0005509); Calcium signaling (GO:0005509) —LEADS_TO→ Long QT interval (HP:0001658); Haploinsufficient variant in CALM1 —DISRUPTS→ CALM1 (HGNC:1304); CALM1 (HGNC:1304) —LEADS_TO→ Disease A phenotype. Gain-of-function variants in CALM1 lead to enhanced calcium signaling, resulting in the prolonged QT interval characteristic of LQTS14. Haploinsufficiency of CALM1, due to other variants, disrupts normal calcium buffering and signaling, leading to the phenotype of Disease A.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of any functional variants in CALM1 in patients with Disease A, or identification of a completely distinct molecular pathway driving Disease A. _(variant: Exome allele frequency > 0.01 for variants in CALM1 associated with Disease A's proposed haploinsufficiency mechanism.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CALM1 and calcium signaling in these distinct cardiac conditions could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting calcium modulation for both LQTS14 and Disease A. For instance, drugs that stabilize calcium channels or reduce calcium influx might be beneficial in both contexts, albeit with different specific targets or efficacy depending on the exact nature of the CALM1 dysfunction.
